cases.scenario_title: AUTH_REQUIRED denial for an outpatient knee MRI
cases.scenario_description: Member M-1001 (Gold plan) had an outpatient knee MRI (MRI-KNEE) denied with reason code AUTH_REQUIRED. The service is a covered benefit that requires prior authorization, and no matching authorization record exists for this member in the synthetic dataset.

required_findings.statement: The claim is DENIED with denial_reason_code AUTH_REQUIRED.
MRI-KNEE is a covered benefit under the member's Gold plan, and that plan's benefit record requires prior authorization for it.
No prior-authorization record exists for member M-1001 for any service in the synthetic dataset (the only two authorization records on file both belong to member M-1002).
Both the servicing provider (PRV-1001, Lakeside Imaging Center) and the ordering provider (PRV-4001, Dr. Ana Kowalski) are in-network -- network participation is not the basis of this denial.

The investigation agent reaches a terminal EVIDENCE_SUFFICIENT status for this claim -- all critical structured-fact categories (member/plan, benefit, servicing provider, ordering provider) are resolved, so the absent authorization is itself the finding, not a data gap that should route to human review.

The brief states plainly, without hedging into false certainty, that AUTH_REQUIRED reflects only the absence of a matching, currently-effective authorization on file at processing time -- and does not by itself mean the service was never authorized at any point (PA-4).

missing_information: No prior-authorization record for member M-1001 covering service MRI-KNEE exists anywhere in the synthetic dataset (data/prior_authorizations.json only has records for member M-1002).
required_uncertainty_or_qualifications: AUTH_REQUIRED reflects the absence of a matching, currently-effective authorization at the time the claim was processed; it does not confirm the service was never authorized at any point (PA-4).
Whether a prior-authorization request was ever submitted for this member/service but is simply not reflected in this dataset is unknown.
verification_or_human_review_actions: Confirm with the ordering physician's office (Dr. Ana Kowalski, PRV-4001) whether a prior-authorization request was ever submitted for this service (PA-5).

If no request was ever submitted: per policy guidance (PA-5, APL-5), submitting a new prior-authorization request can sometimes resolve this faster than a formal appeal -- this is a suggested next step to consider, not a required or guaranteed one, and a formal appeal remains available, particularly if the member is disputing the underlying denial determination itself rather than missing paperwork.
unsupported_or_prohibited_conclusions: Must not state or imply the claim will be approved, paid, or that the denial will be reversed.
Must not state that prior authorization was 'never obtained' as a settled fact -- only that no matching record was found in the available data.
Must not recommend or estimate any specific dollar payment outcome.

Must not present 'submit a new prior-authorization request' as the only or guaranteed next step -- PA-5 and APL-5 both hedge this as something that 'can sometimes'/'may' help, never a certainty, and a formal appeal remains a legitimate path a member can choose.
known_ambiguities_or_questions_for_human: Whether the member or provider ever attempted to submit a prior-authorization request is not observable from the synthetic dataset and needs provider-office follow-up outside this tool.
cases.review_notes: Module 6 correction: the original wording ('the next step is submitting a new prior-authorization request, not proceeding directly to a formal appeal') was too categorical relative to its own cited sources -- PA-5 says a missing authorization 'can SOMETIMES be resolved' by a new request, and APL-5 says a new request 'MAY be faster' and frames appeal-first as appropriate when the underlying determination (not just paperwork) is disputed. Reworded to match that hedged, conditional source language and added an explicit prohibited-conclusion entry against overclaiming this as a guaranteed/required step. Still pending human review -- this correction does not itself constitute review or approval.

cases.scenario_title: Paid knee MRI with an authorization history containing one expired and one applicable record
cases.scenario_description: Member M-1002 (Gold plan) had an outpatient knee MRI (MRI-KNEE) paid, with billed $1,800.00 and allowed $1,200.00. Two authorization records exist for this member/service: PA-1501 (EXPIRED, 2025 window) and PA-2001 (APPROVED, 2026-01-01 to 2026-06-30).

required_findings.statement: The claim status is PAID with no denial_reason_code recorded.
Two prior-authorization records exist for this member/service: PA-1501 (EXPIRED, effective 2025-01-01 to 2025-06-30) and PA-2001 (APPROVED, effective 2026-01-01 to 2026-06-30).

PA-2001's effective window (2026-01-01 to 2026-06-30) covers the claim's date of service (2026-02-12); PA-1501's window (2025-01-01 to 2025-06-30) does not -- PA-2001 is the record applicable to this claim, per the date-window rule in PA-3, without characterizing PA-1501 as irrelevant to the member's authorization history.
Both the servicing provider (PRV-1001) and ordering provider (PRV-4003, Dr. Morgan Diaz) are in-network.
The investigation agent reaches a terminal EVIDENCE_SUFFICIENT status for this claim.

The brief explicitly declines to explain the $600.00 difference between billed and allowed amount, stating that no fee-schedule or pricing data is available, rather than guessing a contractual reason.

missing_information: No fee-schedule, contracted-rate, or pricing-methodology data is available anywhere in this dataset to explain why the allowed amount ($1,200.00) differs from the billed amount ($1,800.00).
required_uncertainty_or_qualifications: The reason the allowed amount is lower than the billed amount is unknown from the available synthetic data and must not be attributed to a guessed specific cause.
verification_or_human_review_actions: If the member disputes the allowed amount itself (as opposed to authorization or coverage), route to whichever team owns fee-schedule/pricing questions -- outside this tool's scope.
unsupported_or_prohibited_conclusions: Must not invent a specific contractual or fee-schedule reason for the billed-vs-allowed difference.
Must not state PA-1501 was irrelevant or erroneous -- it is a valid historical record, simply outside this claim's date-of-service window.
known_ambiguities_or_questions_for_human: Whether the $600.00 reduction reflects a standard network discount or something else cannot be determined from the available synthetic data.

cases.scenario_title: SERVICE_NOT_COVERED denial for a basic lab panel under a Silver plan
cases.scenario_description: Member M-1003 (Silver plan) had a basic lab panel (LAB-BASIC) denied with reason code SERVICE_NOT_COVERED. The plan's benefit record explicitly and authoritatively marks this service as not covered -- this is a present, resolved determination, not missing data.

required_findings.statement: The claim is DENIED with denial_reason_code SERVICE_NOT_COVERED.
A benefit record exists for LAB-BASIC under the Silver plan and explicitly marks it as not covered (covered=false) -- an authoritative, present determination, not an absent record.

LAB-BASIC does not require prior authorization, and the servicing provider (PRV-1002, QuickDraw Labs) and ordering provider (PRV-4002, Dr. Sam Rivera) are both in-network -- neither authorization nor network status is the basis of this denial.
The investigation agent reaches a terminal EVIDENCE_SUFFICIENT status for this claim.

The brief clearly distinguishes 'not a covered benefit under this plan' (a confirmed, present determination) from 'coverage unknown' -- and does not describe LAB-BASIC's no-prior-auth status as if it were relevant to why the claim was denied.

missing_information: No prior-authorization record exists for member M-1003, though prior authorization is not required for LAB-BASIC and is not the basis of this denial.
required_uncertainty_or_qualifications: This is an authoritative, present 'not covered' determination (BEN-SILVER-LAB-BASIC, covered=false) -- must never be phrased as if coverage is unknown or unresolved.
verification_or_human_review_actions: If the member believes this service should be covered under their Silver plan, the available path is a formal appeal referencing the specific benefit determination (APL-2) -- not a new prior-authorization request, since authorization is not the issue here.
unsupported_or_prohibited_conclusions: Must not suggest submitting a prior-authorization request as a remedy -- this service does not require one and doing so would not change the coverage determination.
Must not imply the denial resulted from a data or system error.
known_ambiguities_or_questions_for_human: None identified -- this case's structured facts and policy basis are fully resolved from the available synthetic data.

cases.scenario_title: OUT_OF_NETWORK_PROVIDER denial for an initial physical therapy visit
cases.scenario_description: Member M-1004 (Gold plan) had an initial physical therapy visit (PT-INITIAL) denied with reason code OUT_OF_NETWORK_PROVIDER. The servicing provider (PRV-2002) is a real, resolved provider record with a confirmed out-of-network status; the service itself is a covered, no-prior-auth-required Gold benefit.

required_findings.statement: The claim is DENIED with denial_reason_code OUT_OF_NETWORK_PROVIDER.
PT-INITIAL is a covered Gold-plan benefit that does not require prior authorization, but is only paid at its standard level when performed in-network.

The servicing provider (PRV-2002, Sunrise Physical Therapy Group) is a real, resolved provider record whose network_status is explicitly 'out-of-network' with no network_name -- this must be described as a confirmed fact about the provider, never as the provider being unidentified, unknown, or unverifiable.
The ordering provider (PRV-4002, Dr. Sam Rivera) is a separate, in-network record -- ordering-provider network status is not the basis of this denial, which concerns the servicing provider only.
The investigation agent reaches a terminal EVIDENCE_SUFFICIENT status for this claim -- an out-of-network servicing provider is a resolved fact, not missing evidence.

The brief does not conflate coverage (benefit_covered=true) with network eligibility (out-of-network) -- these are presented as independent determinations (NET-3), not as contradictory or confusing facts.

missing_information: No network-participation record links PRV-2002 to any network (network_name=null) -- this reflects the provider's genuine lack of a network contract, not a data gap.
required_uncertainty_or_qualifications: Whether the member had a reasonable in-network alternative, or whether any out-of-network exception applies (e.g., an emergency circumstance per NET-3), is not stated anywhere in the available synthetic data and must not be assumed either way.
verification_or_human_review_actions: If the member disputes the network-status determination itself or believes an exception should apply, the appropriate path is a formal appeal referencing this specific claim (APL-2), since this is a plan determination being disputed, not missing paperwork (APL-5).
Confirm PRV-2002's network status against the current provider directory before finalizing any explanation to the member, since network status can change over time (NET-4).
unsupported_or_prohibited_conclusions: Must not state or imply that PRV-2002 could not be found or identified -- it is a fully resolved provider record; only its network participation is negative.
Must not recommend a prior-authorization request as a remedy -- PT-INITIAL does not require one, and the denial reason is unrelated to authorization.
known_ambiguities_or_questions_for_human: Whether any out-of-network exception circumstance applies to this specific visit is not observable from the available data.

cases.scenario_title: Denial with no recorded reason code and multiple genuinely missing records
cases.scenario_description: Member M-1005 (Bronze plan) had a specialist visit (SPECIALIST-VISIT) denied, but no denial_reason_code is recorded, no benefit record exists for PLAN-BRONZE + SPECIALIST-VISIT, and no provider record exists for the claim's own recorded servicing provider_id (PRV-9999). This is the one original case that must route to human review rather than a resolved finding.

required_findings.statement: The claim is DENIED but has no denial_reason_code recorded at all.
No benefit record exists for plan_id=PLAN-BRONZE + service_code=SPECIALIST-VISIT -- a genuine absence, structurally distinct from CLM-1003's present-but-not-covered determination.

No provider record exists for provider_id=PRV-9999, this claim's own recorded servicing provider -- the servicing provider cannot be identified at all, which is a different and weaker claim than 'out-of-network'.
The ordering provider (PRV-4004, Dr. Casey Kim) IS a resolvable, in-network record -- only the servicing side is missing, and this resolved fact should still be reported.
The investigation agent reaches a terminal NEEDS_REVIEW status for this claim -- two of the four critical structured-fact categories (benefit, servicing provider) are unresolved.
AgentResult.missing_information is non-empty. This is a STRUCTURAL check only (list length > 0) -- it does not, on its own, confirm the list's entries are about the right things.

Separately from f6's structural non-emptiness check: AgentResult.missing_information's entries substantively address the source-supported omissions this case actually has -- specifically (1) no benefit record for PLAN-BRONZE + SPECIALIST-VISIT and (2) no provider record for PRV-9999. Confirming this requires reading the list's actual content, not matching a keyword or exact string, and is listed here as its own qualitative finding rather than folded into f6's pass/fail.

The brief does not guess or imply any specific denial reason, coverage outcome, or network status for this claim anywhere -- it states each absence as an absence and recommends escalation instead of resolving the case.

missing_information: No claim-level denial_reason_code is recorded for CLM-1005.
No benefit record exists for plan_id=PLAN-BRONZE + service_code=SPECIALIST-VISIT in data/benefits.json.
No provider record exists for provider_id=PRV-9999 (this claim's own recorded servicing provider) in data/providers.json.
No prior-authorization record exists for member M-1005.
required_uncertainty_or_qualifications: Whether SPECIALIST-VISIT is a covered benefit under PLAN-BRONZE at all is unknown -- the absence of a benefit record is not evidence of non-coverage (contrast CLM-1003, where a present record explicitly states covered=false).

Whether provider PRV-9999 is in-network, out-of-network, or does not exist as a real provider at all is unknown -- the absence of a directory record is not evidence of out-of-network status (contrast CLM-1004, where the provider record exists and explicitly states out-of-network).
The actual basis for this denial is unknown from the available synthetic data and must not be guessed from the service type or from patterns seen in other cases.
verification_or_human_review_actions: Escalate to manual review to obtain or confirm the missing benefit record and servicing-provider identity before any explanation is given to the member (CLM-5, BEN-5).
Confirm the correct servicing-provider identity/ID directly, since PRV-9999 does not resolve to any record in the current provider directory.
unsupported_or_prohibited_conclusions: Must not state or imply any specific denial reason (e.g., not covered, out-of-network, authorization required) since none is recorded and none can be derived.
Must not state PRV-9999 is out-of-network, unlicensed, or otherwise characterize it beyond 'not found in the available provider directory.'
Must not treat the missing benefit or provider records as a final coverage or network denial in either direction.
known_ambiguities_or_questions_for_human: What the correct servicing-provider identity was, and whether PRV-9999 is a data-entry error or a provider genuinely absent from the directory.
Whether a benefit record for PLAN-BRONZE + SPECIALIST-VISIT should exist and was simply never created, versus this combination being intentionally excluded.
What the actual, intended denial reason was, given denial_reason_code was never populated.
